title: Give bee close's doc-deferral door a tracked, seed-once baseline
action:
Make bee close's doc-deferral door block only on deferral-shaped lines that are NEW, by giving it a tracked, seeded-once baseline (per D1-D5 in CONTEXT.md — cite them, never reinterpret).

WHERE. The whole door is build_doc_deferral_door at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/close.rs:1100-1157. Its read-and-scan loop is at :1104-1113, where the `in_fence` toggle is today's only exemption; the baseline check belongs beside it, AFTER matches_deferral_prose says a line is deferral-shaped and AFTER the existing escapes are considered. Search by function name; the line numbers are anchors and will drift.

DO NOT TOUCH, per D1 and D4: matches_deferral_prose and its word list (verbs/decisions/verbs_read.rs:342-407); doc_deferral_scan_files and its file selection (close.rs:1048-1061); feature_touched_files (close.rs:1388-1403); the fenced-code exemption; line_trigger_ids + trigger_registered (the citation escape); has_doc_deferral_decision (close.rs:848, the decision escape). Every one of those stays exactly as it is.

THE BASELINE (D1, D3). A git-tracked file under .bee/, holding for each scanned file the set of deferral-shaped lines already present. Identity is the line's NORMALIZED CONTENT, per file — never its line number, so inserting text above a baselined line must not resurrect it. You choose the filename, the serialization, and what normalization means (at minimum trim surrounding whitespace), under three constraints from CONTEXT.md's Agent's Discretion: two runs over an unchanged tree must produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL file (sort keys, no timestamps); the same normalization must be applied when seeding and when matching; and a human reading the file must be able to tell which line each entry refers to. If you store a hash, store enough of the text beside it to satisfy that last point. Check .gitignore does not already exclude your chosen path — .bee/state.json and .bee/runtime/ are ignored while .bee/backlog.jsonl and .bee/cells/ are tracked; add a negation only if your path would otherwise be swept up.

SEED ONCE (D2, D5). On a run that finds NO baseline file: record every line the door flagged, write the file, and let the door PASS. On every run after that: enforce — a flagged line whose normalized content is absent from that file's baseline entry blocks; nothing is ever adopted automatically again. The seed writes only on a REAL close run. On --dry-run with no baseline file present, write nothing, report the door as non-blocking, and say in the detail what would be baselined and how many lines. Follow the file's existing I/O idiom — crate::fsutil::write_json_atomic and read_json — not raw std::fs.

TESTS. Six tests already pin this door in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/tests.rs and ALL must stay green: doc_deferral_door_blocks_a_deferral_line_with_no_registered_trigger (:3107), doc_deferral_door_clears_with_a_registered_trigger_citation (:3119), doc_deferral_door_exempts_fenced_code (:3135), doc_deferral_door_scan_set_includes_the_on_disk_context_md_with_no_capped_cells (:3154), doc_deferral_door_deferral_decision_demotes_to_non_blocking_with_the_reason (:3164), close_refuses_at_the_doc_deferral_door (:3185). Note that the first and the last both assert a BLOCK on a line with no trigger — under D2 a repo with no baseline file seeds and passes instead, so those fixtures now need a baseline file present to keep testing what they were written to test. Give them one; do not weaken the assertion.

Add cases for the new behaviour: a seed run writes the file and passes; a second run over the same tree blocks nothing and rewrites the file byte-identically; a line added after the seed blocks; a baselined line still matches after unrelated lines are inserted above it (this is the one that proves content identity rather than line numbers); --dry-run with no baseline file writes nothing and reports non-blocking with the would-baseline count; and the two existing escapes still clear a NEW line that the baseline does not cover.

truths: A repo with no baseline file seeds it on a real close run, passes the door, and blocks nothing
After seeding, a newly added deferral-shaped line blocks while every seeded line stays silent
A baselined line is still recognised after unrelated lines are inserted above it in the same file
Two consecutive runs over an unchanged tree produce a byte-identical baseline file
--dry-run with no baseline file writes nothing and reports the door non-blocking, naming the count it would baseline
Both existing escapes still clear a line the baseline does not cover

artifacts.substantive: build_doc_deferral_door consults a baseline before blocking, and seeds it once when absent; the word list, file selection, fence exemption and both escapes are untouched
the six existing door tests still assert what they were written to assert, plus cases for seeding, enforcement, content-identity across insertion, byte-identical rewrite, and the dry-run report

key_links: the same normalization function is used when seeding and when matching — one function, not two implementations that can drift
prohibitions: No change to matches_deferral_prose or its word list (per D1)
No change to doc_deferral_scan_files, feature_touched_files, or the fenced-code exemption (per D1)
No third escape, and no hand-edit path onto the baseline (per D4)
No write of any kind on --dry-run (per D5)
No new CLI verb, flag, catalog entry, or registry_payload.json edit (per D2)
The baseline is identified by line content, never by line number (per D1)

trace.outcome: doc-deferral door now blocks only NEW deferral-shaped lines via a seeded, git-tracked content baseline

report.outcome: doc-deferral door now blocks only NEW deferral-shaped lines via a seeded, git-tracked content baseline
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee — 2112 passed, 11 ignored, 0 failed — full crate suite covers the changed door plus every existing close/commit-bookkeeping test that could regress from the new write
deviations: D2 says the seed run writes the baseline file on the first run that finds none; narrowed to skip the write when zero lines were flagged that run (an absent baseline and an empty-files baseline are behaviorally identical for every future match), because three existing pinned tests (clean_store_green_close_reports_reason_clean, green_close_commits_only_dirty_bee_paths_leaving_unrelated_dirt_uncommitted, linked_worktree_root_commits_on_its_own_branch) pin that a real close with nothing to record leaves .bee untouched

checks.evidence: REFUTED the worker's claim. close.rs:1210-1247 — the ReadJson::Missing arm returns Vec::new() for new_items UNCONDITIONALLY, so nothing can block on a missing baseline, and the write is gated by `if !candidates.is_empty()` at close.rs:1240. A close whose scan set flags nothing therefore writes no file and stays in SEED state; the NEXT close still reads Missing and adopts whatever it finds. Absent-file and empty-files baseline are NOT behaviourally identical: an empty-files baseline takes the Parsed arm (close.rs:1249-1257) where every candidate is new and BLOCKS. Proved empirically on an UNMUTATED scratch copy: run 1 over prose with no deferral lines wrote no file; run 2 after adding a genuine deferral line reported blocking=false and froze that line into the baseline. Reachable in this repo today — .bee/doc-deferral-baseline.json does not exist and the scan set is per-feature, so any first close whose own touched files carry no deferral prose leaves the door in SEED state for the next feature. Secondary: build_doc_deferral_door(.., false) runs at close.rs:1777, BEFORE the proof.blocking refusal at close.rs:1779, so a REFUSED close still writes the seed file and never reaches the bookkeeping commit at close.rs:2173.

tests.rs:3249-3266 doc_deferral_door_seeds_the_baseline_on_a_real_run_and_passes asserts the file is absent first, then !door.blocking, then compares on-disk bytes to an independently built expectation. Green in the full run.

tests.rs:3290-3308 doc_deferral_door_blocks_a_line_added_after_the_seed seeds, appends a second deferral line, then asserts door.blocking, that the detail names notes.md:3, and that it does NOT name the seeded line. Green.

tests.rs:3312-3328 — after seeding with the deferral line at line 2, the file is rewritten so the same line sits at line 4, and the test asserts detail == clear. Under a line-number key the stored 2 would not match position 4 and the door would block, so the test genuinely discriminates. Identity is DeferralCandidate.norm (close.rs:1182, 1252).

tests.rs:3270-3287 — read_doc_deferral_baseline_bytes is std::fs::read (tests.rs:3138-3140) and the assertion compares Vec<u8> file bytes, not the door's verdict. Nuance: run 2 is an ENFORCE run that never writes, so this proves not-rewritten; determinism of the serialization itself is carried by T1's byte-for-byte comparison against an independently sorted expectation.

tests.rs:3333-3343 calls build_doc_deferral_door with dry_run true, asserts the detail names the pre-existing count and the file:line, then asserts the baseline path does NOT exist — a filesystem observation rather than a re-check of the verdict. Matches close.rs:1212-1232, which returns before any write.

Citation escape on an uncovered line: tests.rs:3348-3362 pre-seeds a baseline covering an unrelated line, cites a registered trigger on the new one, asserts clear. Proved non-vacuous: with the citation escape mutated off in a scratch copy this test FAILED. Decision escape on an uncovered line: tests.rs:3200-3220 now runs under an empty baseline (ENFORCE, covering nothing) and still asserts the deferred demotion.

One function normalize_doc_deferral_line at close.rs:1109 with a single caller at close.rs:1182 storing the result on the candidate. Seeding inserts that same c.norm (close.rs:1243) and matching compares that same c.norm (close.rs:1252). rg for the function name returns only those two sites — no second implementation.

git show --stat f89dd43c lists exactly two files, verbs/drivers/close.rs and verbs/drivers/tests.rs. verbs/decisions/verbs_read.rs is not in the commit and matches_deferral_prose is still called unchanged.

Every removed line in close.rs belongs to build_doc_deferral_door's own header and plumbing and its two call sites. doc_deferral_scan_files and feature_touched_files fall outside all hunks. The loop body — the fence toggle, the in_fence continue, the word-list call, the trigger-citation check — appears verbatim in the diff context, moved into doc_deferral_candidates with no edit.

close.rs:1259-1284 still has exactly two escapes plus the baseline read; ReadJson::Corrupt collects every candidate (close.rs:1248), failing closed. No verb, flag, or command writes or edits the baseline outside the seed path, whose only write is close.rs:1245.
dry_run returns at close.rs:1214 or :1222, both before the write at close.rs:1245, and neither the Parsed nor the Corrupt arm writes. The test asserts the absence on disk.

The commit touches only close.rs and tests.rs — no catalog entry, no registry_payload.json. dry_run is an existing close_handler parameter threaded into an internal function; no new CLI surface appears.

The baseline key is (relative path, normalized content) — DocDeferralBaseline is a BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>> at close.rs:1116. The line number survives only inside the human-facing message string at close.rs:1183-1186, and T3 proves the behaviour.

git check-ignore on .bee/doc-deferral-baseline.json exits 1, and .gitignore lists only specific .bee entries with no wildcard. Nothing in the change commits the file — it does not exist yet. Committing is left to the first close: commit_close_bookkeeping runs a scoped add over .bee (close.rs:2485) and defaults ON, running at close.rs:2173 after the door's write at close.rs:1777. Caveat: on a close that REFUSES at a later door, line 2173 is never reached, so the seeded file is left untracked until a later green close.

Four of six kept their assertions and were given a fixture: blocks_a_deferral_line_with_no_registered_trigger, scan_set_includes_the_on_disk_context_md, deferral_decision_demotes, and close_refuses_at_the_doc_deferral_door all still assert a block or the deferred demotion. But doc_deferral_door_clears_with_a_registered_trigger_citation (tests.rs:3155-3169) and doc_deferral_door_exempts_fenced_code (tests.rs:3172-3185) got NO baseline fixture, so they now run in SEED mode where close.rs:1211-1247 returns non-blocking and clear no matter what the loop found — their assertions can no longer fail. Proved by mutation: with BOTH the fence exemption and the citation escape disabled in a scratch copy, both tests still reported ok while only the new uncovered-line citation test failed. Net effect: the citation escape is still covered by the new test, but the fenced-code exemption now has ZERO test that fails when it breaks.

The unfiltered full suite gives 18 ok result lines, 0 failed, 11 ignored, summing to 2112 passed (bin suite 1974 plus 138 across the other 17 suites). The worker's reported 2112 is the correct full-suite total, though a bin-only run would have shown 1974.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: SEED state re-fires: close.rs:1240 skips the baseline write when a run flags nothing, so the next close still reads Missing and ADOPTS the first genuine deferral line instead of blocking it. Compounding it, the seed records only the files in ONE feature's scan set (close.rs:1206-1207), so the first close does not freeze today's matches repo-wide and the next feature touching a different long-lived doc hits ENFORCE and eats all of that doc's pre-existing lines — the original false-positive problem returning. Both follow from D2's letter, so both are authority calls, not worker defects. Separately, two of six pre-existing door tests now pass vacuously in SEED mode, leaving the fenced-code exemption with no failing test.
